# ui::Callback

Header: `winui/core/Callback.hpp`.

```cpp
template <typename Sig> class Callback
```

The one handler type: a `std::move_only_function`, so a handler may capture a `std::unique_ptr`. Spell the signature at the use site (`Callback<void(bool)>`, `Callback<void(std::size_t)>`), so a reader sees the payload without chasing a typedef.

A handler with a payload also takes a lambda that takes nothing, for when only the event matters: `.on_selection_changed = [&] { refresh(); }`. A handler that returns a [ui::Handling](namespace-ui.md#handling) or a [ui::Decision](namespace-ui.md#decision) also takes a lambda that returns nothing, which gets the event's default.

Example: 
```cpp
auto dialog = std::make_unique<std::string>("owned state"); // any move-only capture works
ui::Callback<void(bool)> on_checked_changed = [owned = std::move(dialog)](bool on) {
    if (on) { std::puts(owned->c_str()); }
};
auto toggle = std::make_unique<ui::ToggleSwitchControl>();
toggle->on_checked_changed(std::move(on_checked_changed));
toggle->on_checked_changed([] { std::puts("toggled"); }); // the payload ignored
```
